in_hebrew.name: חקון
in_hebrew.long_meaning: From the Hebrew root 'chakah' which means 'to be right, correct, or wise.' This name is derived from the term 'hakam' meaning 'sage, scholar, or wise man.' In the biblical context, it could also mean 'the one who is just and righteous.'

in_greek.name: Ακακος
in_greek.long_meaning: From the Greek word 'akakos' which means 'pure, innocent, or blameless.' This name is derived from the root 'akos' meaning 'blameless.' In the biblical context, it could also mean 'the one who is without guilt or reproach.'

in_latin.name: Hakon
in_latin.long_meaning: From the Latin word 'sapiens' meaning 'wise.' This name is derived from the root 'sapere' meaning 'to taste or perceive wisely.' In the biblical context, it could also mean 'the one who is discerning and understanding.'
